first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both declining, and inherited evidence indicates that reducing onboarding friction improves completion, time-to-value, and SMB activation. This directly addresses the current funnel weakness without the known 30-day retention harm associated with promotional pricing. Verify both supporting records and measure qualified revenue and retention as downstream guardrails.

final.rationale: Run a shorter, lower-friction onboarding experiment, prioritizing SMB users while preserving segment-level analysis. The verified onboarding result improved completion by 13%, reduced time-to-value by 2.1 days, and increased 30-day retention by 3%. Signup simplification also raised SMB activation by 9% and qualified revenue by 4%, directly matching the current declines. Because signup simplification had a 1% retention decline and was not validated outside SMB, retain 30-day retention and qualified revenue as guardrails and avoid broad rollout until results confirm sustainable value.
